title: Map Rubric Sub-Criteria to Analysis Outputs Before Coding
when_to_use: When the task instructions reference a scoring rubric or evaluation criteria.
experience:
Markdown bullets: 
- Extract all specific sub-criteria (e.g., formulas, required tables, significance tests) from the rubric before writing any code.
- Create a checklist mapping each sub-criterion to a planned output (e.g., '1.2.A.1 requires computing share_high_disease per level; define formula').
- Validate that all required metrics, units, and annotations (e.g., p-values, confidence intervals) are explicitly planned.
- Before finalizing, cross-check each analysis output against the rubric checklist to ensure all items are addressed.
- If a rubric criterion involves multiple steps (e.g., winsorization, anomaly handling), implement and report each step separately.
checklist: Map each sub-criterion to a specific analysis component
Verify required outputs (tables, formulas, tests) are planned
Implement and report each step explicitly
common_failure_prevented: Missing required analysis components (e.g., winsorization, significance tests, specific tables) because the agent dove into exploratory coding without aligning with the rubric.

title: Formalize Statistical Tests and Effect Sizes for Comparisons
when_to_use: When the analysis task involves comparing groups (e.g., across disaster levels) or assessing relationships.
experience:
Markdown bullets: 
- Determine the appropriate statistical test (e.g., ANOVA for parametric, Kruskal-Wallis for non-parametric) based on data distribution and group number.
- Always report test statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, and effect size (e.g., eta-squared for ANOVA).
- For post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey HSD, Dunn-Bonferroni), report adjusted p-values and confidence intervals.
- Annotate findings with statistical evidence (e.g., 'F(3,96)=5.21, p<0.01, η²=0.14').
- Check assumptions (normality, homogeneity of variances) and report if robust methods are used.
checklist: Report test statistic, df, p-value, effect size
Conduct and report post-hoc pairwise tests
common_failure_prevented: Reporting observed differences (e.g., 'Level 5 has highest disease risk') without supporting statistical tests, p-values, or effect sizes.

title: Design Actionable Recommendations with Trigger Thresholds and Ownership
when_to_use: When the task requires providing targeted recommendations or interventions.
experience:
Markdown bullets: 
- Structure recommendations as a matrix linking conditions (e.g., disaster level/type) to specific actions.
- For each action, define a clear, measurable trigger threshold (e.g., 'Disease Risk > 40%').
- Assign a responsible party (role or team) and a deadline (e.g., 'within 48 hours').
- Include resource dependencies (e.g., inventory, personnel) and priority rules (e.g., 'allocate X if Y').
- Validate recommendations against constraints (budget, logistics) and conduct sensitivity analysis if needed.
checklist: List resource dependencies and priority rules
common_failure_prevented: Providing generic advice (e.g., 'improve disease surveillance') without specific triggers, ownership, or actionable steps.
